text:
Canvix

 Design anything. Free for everyone. 

Free & open-source graphic design tool — a community-built Canva alternative.

 
 
 
 
 
 

Features · Quick start · Self-hosting · Roadmap · Contributing

 

---

 ✨ What is Canvix?

Canvix is a browser-based design tool that lets anyone create social media posts,
presentations, posters, logos and thumbnails — with a drag-and-drop editor, a
366-template library and one-click export. It runs entirely on your own infrastructure, stores designs
in your own database, and exports files locally in your browser. Free accounts
keep your designs yours; anonymous link-editing keeps working too. No
watermarks, no paywalls.

 🆓 Free forever — the promise

 Every feature in Canvix is free, and it stays free. Forever. There is no
Pro tier, no subscription, no trial countdown, no watermark ransom, no
"premium" element you can drag but not drop. The whole point of this project
is a design tool that never asks you for a credit card:

- All 366 templates — including the entire premium collection — are free
- All exports (PNG, JPG, WebP, SVG, PDF, PPTX, video, GIF) are free and unwatermarked
- All AI features (magic edit, magic write, background removal, translate)
 run against your own API keys, so there is nothing for us to meter
- Accounts are free — username + password, no email, no verification,
 no external provider; a self-hoster runs the whole thing for $0
- Self-hosting is first-class: your server, your database, your rules
- The license is MIT — you can even fork it and build a business on it

If anyone ever asks you to pay for Canvix, you are being scammed: the source
is right here.

 🎨 Features

 v0.9.0 — Accounts & per-design ownership

- Free accounts, zero dependencies — username + password with scrypt
 hashing from node:crypto and opaque DB-backed sessions (HttpOnly,
 SameSite=Lax cookies; the DB stores only sha256(token) so a leak never
 yields usable sessions). No email, no OAuth, no external provider —
 deliberately self-contained so self-hosting stays free forever.
- Per-design ownership — designs you create while signed in are private
 to your account: the dashboard scopes to “yours + shared”, and every
 mutating API (save, delete, restore, version snapshot) answers 403 for
 anyone else. Share links still open — in view-only mode with an honest
 banner in the editor.
- Nothing breaks for existing setups — ownerless designs keep the exact
 pre-v0.9 link-editable behaviour. One click ( “Save my designs to this
 account” ) migrates the designs this browser created into your new
 account — anonymous creations are attributed to the creating browser
 ( canvix anon cookie, sha256-hashed in the DB), so adopt-all can
 never sweep up another person's work . Legacy designs from before
 attribution exist? Claim those one-by-one with the per-design
 “Save to my account” action (a deliberate, visible action for
 pre-accounts self-hosters).
- CSRF-safe writes — every mutating API route enforces same-origin on
 top of the SameSite=Lax session cookie; cross-site POST/PUT/DELETE
 requests answer 403 CSRF REJECTED . Non-browser clients (curl, the MCP
 endpoint) are unaffected.
- Collab identity upgrade — signed-in users appear under their real
 username in presence, cursors and comments.
- DNS-rebinding pinning (SSRF close-out) — the MCP server's safeFetch 
 now connects via a custom lookup pinned to the validated IP, closing the
 TOCTOU window documented in v0.6.1. TLS keeps the real hostname for SNI,
 so certificate validation is unaffected.
- End-to-end CI verification — the “Canvix Database Setup” workflow now
 boots the built server against your real database and exercises the whole
 account + ownership + claim-safety + CSRF flow (register → me → owned
 create → owner save → anonymous 403 → logout → revoked-token replay →
 login → cross-origin rejection → two-browser adopt-all scoping →
 cross-account isolation) before cleaning up after itself.

 v0.8.0 — Supabase-ready infrastructure & the 110-template library

- Supabase-first database support — switching hosts (Neon → Supabase,
 or anything else) is now a two-command move:
 - Real migrations — prisma/migrations ships in the repo, so
 npm run db:setup creates the full schema on a brand-new database
 (Supabase, Neon, RDS, local…) and seeds the template library in one go
 - Self-healing setup — if your database was provisioned with the
 pre-v0.8 db push flow, db:setup detects it, baselines the migration
 history (Prisma's documented path) and continues instead of dead-ending
 - Smart connection handling ( src/lib/db-url.ts ) — a copy-pasted
 Supabase connection string just works: TLS is auto-required for remote
 hosts, and the transaction pooler (port 6543) automatically gets
 pgbouncer-compatible settings so prepared statements don't break
 - /api/health — a one-page diagnosis of env → connectivity →
 migration → seed, with the exact fix printed at each step
 - Actionable errors everywhere — “Could not open template” is dead:
 API failures now carry classified codes ( DB NOT MIGRATED ,
 DB UNREACHABLE …), the dashboard shows a setup banner with the fix,
 and toasts tell you exactly what to run
- The template library, ×1.8 — now 110 templates, all free — 50 new
 2026-trend originals across every category, authored in-house (podcast
 quote card, new-listing post, bootcamp, restaurant special, lookbook,
 webinar, LinkedIn banner, recipe pin, birthday story, Black Friday,
 playlist cover, flash-sale countdown, grand opening · investor pitch,
 marketing plan, course, agency portfolio, quarterly review, demo day,
 nonprofit impact, product launch · wedding invitation, gym flyer, cafe
 menu, concert poster, yoga flyer, gift certificate, business card, open
 mic, moving sale · executive & creative resumes, cover letter, proposal,
 invoice, newsletter, whitepaper, agenda, press release · 7 thumbnails ·
 3 logos). The library lives in src/lib/templates/ as collections so it
 can keep growing, and a validator

install.title: Quick start
install.html:
Prerequisites: Node.js 20+ (or Bun), and a PostgreSQL database — a free Supabase project is the easiest start (any other Postgres works too: Neon, RDS, Docker, local).

git clone https://github.com/mir-ashiq/canvix.git
cd canvix
npm install            # or: bun install

# set up the database (get a connection string first — see below)
cp .env.example .env   # then edit DATABASE_URL
npm run db:setup       # migrations + 110 free templates, in one command

npm run dev            # → http://localhost:3000

Getting your Supabase connection string: Supabase dashboard → Connect (or Project Settings → Database) → copy the URI. Both styles work out of the box — Canvix auto-applies the right flags:

Style Looks like Notes
Transaction pooler (recommended) …pooler.supabase.com:6543/postgres IPv4-friendly; Canvix auto-adds pgbouncer=true&connection_limit=1
Direct connection db.<ref>.supabase.co:5432/postgres IPv6-only on most plans — use it only if your host has an IPv6 route

Replace [YOUR-PASSWORD] with your database password, and you're done. If anything looks off later, open /api/health on your server — it checks env → connectivity → migrations → seed and prints the exact fix.

Production build:

npm run build
npm run start

v0.8.0 — Supabase-ready infrastructure & the 110-template library
  • Supabase-first database support — switching hosts (Neon → Supabase, or anything else) is now a two-command move:
    • Real migrations — prisma/migrations ships in the repo, so npm run db:setup creates the full schema on a brand-new database (Supabase, Neon, RDS, local…) and seeds the template library in one go
    • Self-healing setup — if your database was provisioned with the pre-v0.8 db push flow, db:setup detects it, baselines the migration history (Prisma's documented path) and continues instead of dead-ending
    • Smart connection handling (src/lib/db-url.ts) — a copy-pasted Supabase connection string just works: TLS is auto-required for remote hosts, and the transaction pooler (port 6543) automatically gets pgbouncer-compatible settings so prepared statements don't break
    • /api/health — a one-page diagnosis of env → connectivity → migration → seed, with the exact fix printed at each step
    • Actionable errors everywhere — “Could not open template” is dead: API failures now carry classified codes (DB_NOT_MIGRATED, DB_UNREACHABLE…), the dashboard shows a setup banner with the fix, and toasts tell you exactly what to run
  • The template library, ×1.8 — now 110 templates, all free — 50 new 2026-trend originals across every category, authored in-house (podcast quote card, new-listing post, bootcamp, restaurant special, lookbook, webinar, LinkedIn banner, recipe pin, birthday story, Black Friday, playlist cover, flash-sale countdown, grand opening · investor pitch, marketing plan, course, agency portfolio, quarterly review, demo day, nonprofit impact, product launch · wedding invitation, gym flyer, cafe menu, concert poster, yoga flyer, gift certificate, business card, open mic, moving sale · executive & creative resumes, cover letter, proposal, invoice, newsletter, whitepaper, agenda, press release · 7 thumbnails · 3 logos). The library lives in src/lib/templates/ as collections so it can keep growing, and a validator (scripts/validate-templates.ts) checks every entry at CI time
v0.7.0 — Fast & Free Forever: rendering performance & the premium template collection
  • Rendering performance — the canvas was rebuilt around three classic hot-path killers, and every one is gone:
    • Structural sharing in the editor store — every mutation now builds only the pages/elements it actually touches; untouched objects keep their identity. A keystroke, a slider drag or a remote/AI live edit re-renders exactly one canvas node instead of the whole scene, and deep-cloning the entire document per edit is history
    • O(1) undo/redo — history snapshots now share structure with live state (like Immer, without Immer): pushing history is a reference copy, and a 60-step history of a large design costs a fraction of the old memory
    • Memoized canvas nodes — ElementNode no longer subscribes to the whole store (it reads actions at event time via getState()), is wrapped in React.memo, and receives stable callbacks — so selection changes, panel toggles and remote cursors don't re-render a single shape
    • Split Konva layers — interaction chrome (transformer, snap guides, marquee, ruler guides, draw preview) moved to its own <canvas> layer: dragging an element no longer repaints the chrome, and guide updates no longer repaint the artwork
    • Snap-guide equality guard — identical guide sets don't trigger a React render; snapping during drag only redraws when something visibly changed
    • Shared image cache — images decode once per URL and are reused across pages, thumbnails and duplicated nodes (with in-flight dedup and a bounded 300-entry LRU)
    • perfectDrawEnabled: false on element nodes — skips Konva's hit-canvas perfection pass during drag/transform for a big interactive win
    • Lazy template thumbnails — preview stages mount via IntersectionObserver (300 px pre-roll), so scrolling the 366-template library stays smooth; only visible cards own a canvas
    • Locked in by tests: src/store/editor-store.test.ts asserts the identity guarantees (untouched pages/elements keep references, history shares structure, snapshots are never mutated in place)
  • The premium template collection — all free — 39 new templates (21 → 60), every one designed to Canva-grade quality and every one unlocked: social (flash sale story, trattoria, open house, bootcamp, webinar, podcast cover, birthday story, wanderlust, LinkedIn banner, minimal quote), presentations (pitch deck noir, quarterly report, webinar deck, course welcome, roadmap, meet-the-team), print (neon gig poster, charity gala, artisan menu, spa voucher, yard sign, luxe card, wedding thank-you, coupon), documents (proposal, newsletter, ebook cover, whitepaper, press release, meeting agenda, studio invoice, case study), thumbnails (gaming, tutorial, podcast episode, unboxing) and logos (orbit, bloom, apex). The templates panel gets a "Premium collection · free forever" section — premium is a quality label here, never a paywall
